briefing.headline: Burnham rejects EU student fee parity, US politics heats up
briefing.overview: The UK government faces pressure over tuition fees for EU students while Welsh devolution issues stir debate. In the US, partisan tensions rise around investigations into the former administration.

stories.title: UK tuition fee stance for EU students
stories.what_happened: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the UK will not offer equal tuition fees for EU students, while negotiations with the European bloc continue. The announcement was made during a press briefing on 25 November.
stories.why_it_matters: The decision tests the government's handling of post‑Brexit relations and domestic education policy, linking to the AQA topic of the Constitution and the executive's powers. It also raises questions about fairness and the UK's international obligations.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Proponents say the policy protects UK taxpayers and reflects sovereign control over education funding.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opponents claim it breaches the spirit of EU agreements and harms EU students' access to UK universities.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Left‑leaning commentators argue the move undermines social equity and the principle of free movement of people.

key_term.definition: The authority of the Prime Minister and Cabinet to make policy decisions without prior parliamentary approval.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence in an essay on the limits of executive power within the UK constitution.

stories.title: Reform UK's failed bid to remove Senedd Presiding Officer
stories.what_happened: Reform UK attempted to oust Senedd Presiding Officer Huw Irranca‑Davies but the motion was defeated 55‑29 on 24 November. The vote followed a viral speech by Plaid Cymru MS Carrie Harper.
stories.why_it_matters: The episode illustrates party dynamics and the role of pressure groups in devolved legislatures, relevant to the AQA topics of parties and devolution. It shows how intra‑parliamentary tactics can shape governance.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Reform UK claims the motion was necessary to hold the Senedd leadership accountable.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opponents say the attempt was politically motivated and destabilised the devolved institution.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservative observers view the defeat as a defence of parliamentary stability over partisan disruption.

key_term.definition: The statutory transfer of powers from the central UK government to regional bodies such as the Welsh Senedd.

stories.exam_use: Cite in a discussion of how party politics operate within devolved legislatures.

stories.title: Navarro warns of civil war over Democratic probes
stories.what_happened: Former trade adviser Peter Navarro warned that Democratic investigations into the Trump administration could lead to a Republican victory in 2028 or spark a 'civil war' on 25 November. He made the comments in a televised interview.
stories.why_it_matters: The statement reflects heightened partisan conflict and the role of Congress in overseeing the executive, linking to the AQA topics of the President, Congress and parties. It also raises issues of political rhetoric and democratic stability.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Navarro’s supporters say the warning highlights the danger of partisan overreach by Democrats.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Critics contend the comment inflames division and undermines democratic norms.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Left‑leaning analysts view the claim as an exaggeration used to deflect accountability.

key_term.definition: The system whereby each branch of government can limit the powers of the others.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence when evaluating the effectiveness of congressional oversight of the executive.

stories.title: Judge blocks Fulton County ballot‑copy order
stories.what_happened: A Georgia judge halted an order requiring Fulton County to hand over seized 2020 ballot copies to the state election board on 25 November. The decision came after a prior order was issued by the same judge.
stories.why_it_matters: The case highlights the judiciary’s role in election disputes, pertinent to the AQA focus on US courts and elections. It also touches on issues of election integrity and federal‑state relations.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Pro‑court advocates say the block protects voter privacy and prevents political interference.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Election‑integrity groups argue the decision hampers transparency in investigating alleged fraud.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservative commentators view the ruling as a defence against partisan overreach by Democrats.

key_term.definition: The process by which courts examine the legality of actions taken by public bodies.

stories.exam_use: Reference in an essay on the courts’ impact on US electoral processes.

stories.title: Sark election sees record turnout
stories.what_happened: Six members were re‑elected to Sark’s Chief Pleas on 25 November, with the island recording its highest voter turnout in 20 years. The election was noted for its peaceful conduct.
stories.why_it_matters: The result offers a concrete example of local electoral participation, linking to the AQA topic of elections and democratic engagement in the UK. It also allows comparison with larger‑scale elections.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Local observers praise the high turnout as evidence of robust civic engagement.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Some argue the small electorate limits the significance of the turnout figure.

perspectives.label: From the centre
perspectives.text: Centrist analysts see the result as typical of micro‑state democratic practice.

key_term.definition: The proportion of eligible voters who cast a ballot in an election.

stories.exam_use: Use to illustrate variations in electoral participation across different political units.
